title: No burning sun, no biting cold.
subtitle: Rest in a climate that never troubles
then: Ibn Kathir says there will be {reward}no disturbing heat and no painful cold, only one climate, always{/reward}, and they will not want it changed. Earlier, the righteous were patient. {idea}Now they recline.{/idea}
now: You check the weather app every morning. Too hot to walk, too cold to go out, the AC bill, the heating bill. {reward}A place where the weather is never a problem is part of the promise.{/reward}
old: Discomfort is just a permanent part of life.
new: Every hot or freezing day here can be borne with a place of rest in mind.
try: Next time the weather annoys you, say: there is a Garden with none of this.

title: Shade close by, fruit that bends down to you.
subtitle: Nothing out of reach
then: Mujahid said {reward}if he stands it rises with him, if he sits it lowers, if he lies down it lowers more.{/reward} Qatadah said {idea}no thorn or distance keeps their hands from it.{/idea}
now: Everything good here seems just out of reach: the promotion, the house, the rest you need. You keep stretching. {reward}In the Garden, what you want comes to you.{/reward}
old: Everything I want, I have to reach and strain for.
new: There is a place where good things bend toward me.
try: Share fruit with someone today, and remember the fruit that bends down.

title: Silver vessels and cups passed around to them.
subtitle: Served, not serving
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}servants will go around them with silver vessels of food and cups of drink.{/reward} These are the same people who, a few verses earlier, {idea}fed the poor, the orphan, and the captive while wanting the food themselves.{/idea}
now: You are the one who always serves: the tea at family gatherings, the plates after Eid dinner, the one who clears the table. {reward}One day the plates come to you.{/reward}
old: Being the one who serves means I am at the bottom.
new: Those who served others here will be served there.
try: Serve someone at your table today before you serve yourself.

title: Silver as clear as glass, filled just right.
subtitle: Measured to your exact thirst
then: Ibn Abbas and others said it is {reward}the whiteness of silver in the transparency of glass{/reward}, something with no likeness in this world. The measure is {idea}exactly what quenches their thirst, not more, not less.{/idea}
now: You pour too much and waste it. You order too little and leave hungry. Nothing here is ever quite right. {reward}The Garden is precise to your need.{/reward}
old: Nothing in life ever fits me exactly.
new: Allah knows my measure. In the Garden it is met exactly.
try: Take only as much as you need at your next meal.

title: A cup mixed with ginger, warm after the cool.
subtitle: Balance in every delight
then: Ibn Kathir says {reward}one time they are given a drink mixed with camphor, which is cool, and another time with ginger, which is warm{/reward}, so their state is balanced. Those nearest to Allah {idea}drink from all of it as they wish.{/idea}
now: Ginger tea on a cold evening, a cold drink at noon. Your body needs both. {reward}The Garden is not just more. It is perfectly balanced.{/reward}
old: Paradise sounds like the same pleasure over and over.
new: The Garden is full of variety and balance, designed with care.
try: Make a cup of something warm today and thank Allah for its taste.

title: A spring there named Salsabil.
subtitle: A spring that never stops flowing
then: Ikrimah said {reward}Salsabil is the name of a spring in Paradise.{/reward} Mujahid said it is called this {idea}because of its continuous flowing and the strength of its current.{/idea}
now: You saved your energy for a weekend that went too fast. Joy here comes in drips: a good day, a good meal, then it is over. {reward}This spring is named for never stopping.{/reward}
new: There is a joy that keeps flowing and never runs dry.
try: When a good moment ends today, ask Allah for the joy that does not end.

title: Servants like scattered pearls, forever young.
subtitle: The beauty of those who serve them
then: Ibn Kathir says they stay {reward}in one state forever, never growing older.{/reward} Seeing them rush to serve, with their beauty and fine clothes, {idea}you would think them scattered pearls{/idea}, and nothing is lovelier than pearls in a beautiful place.
now: You notice your first grey hairs in the bathroom mirror. Your kids grow, your parents slow down. {reward}The Garden is a place where time stops taking.{/reward}
old: Losing youth and beauty is just how it is.
new: Nothing in the Garden fades. What is lost here is not lost forever.
try: Use one hour of your health today for something that lasts.

title: Look there, and you see delight and a great kingdom.
subtitle: Even the least of them gets ten worlds
then: Ibn Kathir cites the authentic hadith: Allah will tell {idea}the last person to leave the Fire and enter Paradise{/idea}, {reward}you have the like of the world and ten times more.{/reward} If that is the least, he asks, what of those higher than him?
now: You compare your flat to your cousin's house, your salary to your friend's. The world feels like a race for a bigger slice. {reward}The smallest place in the Garden is bigger than the whole world, ten times over.{/reward}
old: I need more of this world to be satisfied.
new: The smallest share there is more than all of this world.
try: The next time you feel envy today, remember the ten worlds.

title: Their Lord gives them a drink that purifies.
subtitle: Beautiful outside, clean inside
then: Ibn Kathir says the drink {reward}purifies their insides of envy, hatred, harm, and every bad trait.{/reward} Ali bin Abi Talib said at the gate of Paradise they will drink from one spring and {idea}Allah will remove whatever harm is inside them.{/idea}
now: You dress well for the wedding and smile at the cousin you secretly resent. The outside is fine. Inside is a knot. {reward}In the Garden there is no knot left.{/reward}
new: Allah cares about a clean heart, and in the Garden He makes it fully clean.
try: Make dua today for someone you feel envy toward.

title: This is your reward. Your effort has been appreciated.
subtitle: Small deeds, large return
then: Ibn Kathir says this will be said {reward}to honor them.{/reward} Allah {idea}rewards a small amount of deeds with a large amount of reward.{/idea} The people who wanted no thanks from anyone in verse 9 are thanked by Allah.
now: You cleaned up after everyone and no one noticed. You stayed up with a sick child and no one knew. {reward}One day you will hear: your effort was appreciated.{/reward}
old: If no one notices my effort, it does not count.
new: Allah notices every effort and repays it far more than it was.
try: Keep going with one unseen effort today, knowing it is seen.
